question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(a), when must a Georgia broker maintain a separate, federally-insured trust or escrow account?
choice_a: Only when the broker personally negotiates a residential sale
choice_b: Only if the brokerage firm has more than five affiliated licensees
choice_d: Whenever the broker or an affiliated licensee accepts down payments, earnest money, security deposits, rents, or association fees belonging to others
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(a) requires a broker who accepts, or whose affiliates accept, down payments, earnest money, security deposits, rents, or association fees to maintain a separate, federally-insured trust account at a Georgia financial institution.

question: A Georgia broker whose firm does not normally handle trust funds unexpectedly receives an earnest money check from a buyer on a rare listing. Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(a), how quickly must the broker open a designated trust account for the funds?
choice_a: Within one business day of receipt
choice_c: By the end of the same renewal period
choice_d: There is no deadline as long as the funds are eventually deposited before closing
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(a) requires a broker who does not normally hold trust funds but later receives some to open a designated trust account within one business day of receipt.

question: A Georgia broker opens a primary trust account and, several months later, opens a second trust account. What notice obligations apply to GREC?
choice_a: No notice is ever required for any trust account as long as it is federally insured
choice_b: The broker must notify GREC of the bank and account name/number for the primary account under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(b), and must notify GREC of the additional account within one month of opening it under Rule 520-1-.08(1)(a)
choice_c: Notice is required only for the first account opened; additional accounts are exempt from any notice requirement
choice_d: The broker has one year to notify GREC of any trust account, primary or additional
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(b) requires the broker to notify GREC of the bank name and account name/number, and Rule 520-1-.08(1)(a) separately requires notice of any additional account within one month of opening it.

question: What examination rights does GREC hold over a broker's trust account under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(c)?
choice_a: GREC may examine a broker's trust account only once, at initial licensure, and never again
choice_b: GREC has no independent examination authority over trust accounts absent a court order
choice_c: GREC may examine the account at any time upon reasonable cause, and separately examines each broker's trust account during each renewal period, or accepts a CPA report or renewal-form summary in lieu of that examination
choice_d: GREC may examine trust accounts only if a written complaint has been filed against the broker
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(c) gives GREC authority to examine a broker's trust account at any time upon reasonable cause, and also provides for examination during each renewal period, which the broker may satisfy with a CPA report or renewal-form summary instead.

question: May a Georgia broker maintain more than one trust account?
choice_a: No -- Georgia law limits every broker to a single trust account regardless of transaction volume
choice_b: Yes, but only with prior written approval from every affiliated licensee
choice_c: Yes, but only if each account is held at a different out-of-state bank
choice_d: Yes -- O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(d) permits a broker to maintain more than one trust account, provided GREC is given notice
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(d) allows a broker to maintain more than one trust account, subject to notifying GREC.

question: A buyer's earnest money is held in a broker's trust account while the sale contract is still pending, well before closing. Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(e), may the broker withdraw any portion of those funds as earned commission at this point?
choice_a: No -- a broker is not entitled to any part of trust funds as commission until the transaction has been consummated or terminated
choice_b: Yes -- the broker may withdraw the commission portion as soon as the contract is signed
choice_c: Yes -- the broker may withdraw up to 50% of the anticipated commission at the broker's discretion
choice_d: Yes -- the broker may withdraw the full commission once the buyer's loan is approved
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(e) states a broker is not entitled to any part of earnest money, security deposits, or other trust funds as commission until the transaction has been consummated or terminated -- a pending, still-open contract does not satisfy that condition.

question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(g), where may a nonresident broker licensed in Georgia keep the required trust account?
choice_a: Nonresident brokers are categorically barred from holding any Georgia trust funds
choice_b: At GREC's discretion, in the broker's home-state bank, subject to GREC's examination rights
choice_c: Only at a bank physically located within Georgia, with no exceptions
choice_d: Only at a federally chartered bank headquartered in Washington, D.C.
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-20(g) allows a nonresident broker, at GREC's discretion, to keep the trust account in their home-state bank, subject to GREC's examination rights.

question: Georgia's Rule 520-1-.08(1) requires a licensee to place trust items into the broker's custody 'as soon after receipt as is practicably possible' and requires the broker to 'promptly deposit' them into the designated trust account. What is notably absent from this Georgia rule compared to many other states?
choice_a: Any requirement that the funds be deposited into a federally-insured account
choice_b: Any requirement that the licensee turn funds over to the broker at all
choice_c: A fixed numeric deadline, such as a specific number of banking days, for depositing trust funds
choice_d: Any distinction between earnest money and security deposits
explanation: Rule 520-1-.08(1)(b)-(c) uses 'promptly' and 'as soon as practicably possible' rather than a specific banking-days count -- Georgia does not impose a fixed numeric deposit-timing deadline the way some other states do.

question: If a Georgia broker's trust account is interest-bearing, what does Rule 520-1-.08(1) require regarding the interest earned?
choice_a: The interest must always be forwarded automatically to GREC
choice_b: The broker may always retain all interest as additional compensation without disclosure
choice_c: Interest-bearing trust accounts are prohibited outright in Georgia
choice_d: A written agreement specifying who is entitled to the interest
explanation: Rule 520-1-.08(1) requires a written agreement on entitlement to interest whenever the trust account is interest-bearing.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.08(1)(e), when may a Georgia broker's own personal funds be placed into the trust account?
choice_a: Only in a clearly identified amount, and only to cover a bank-required minimum balance or service charges on the account, with withdrawals of those broker funds made by checks payable to the broker
choice_b: Freely, whenever the broker needs short-term working capital
choice_c: Never, under any circumstance, even to cover bank service charges
choice_d: Only during the first 30 days after the account is opened
explanation: Rule 520-1-.08(1)(e) allows commingling of the broker's own funds only in a clearly identified amount to cover a bank-required minimum balance or service charges, with withdrawals made by checks payable to the broker.

question: What level of detail must a Georgia broker's trust account accounting system capture under Rule 520-1-.08(2)?
choice_a: Only the total monthly deposits and withdrawals, without transaction-level detail
choice_b: Buyer and seller names, the deposit amount and date, the property involved, and each disbursement check's amount, payee, and date
choice_c: Only the bank's monthly statement, with no additional broker recordkeeping
choice_d: Only the closing attorney's settlement statement
explanation: Rule 520-1-.08(2) requires an accounting system detailing buyer/seller names, deposit amount and date, the property, and each disbursement check's amount, payee, and date.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.08(6), how often must a Georgia broker reconcile trust account records against the bank balance, and how long must those reconciliation records be retained?
choice_a: A written reconciliation is required only annually, and records need be kept for 1 year
choice_b: Reconciliation is required only at license renewal, and records need not be retained at all
choice_c: A monthly written reconciliation is required, and the records must be retained for 3 years
choice_d: A weekly reconciliation is required, with permanent (indefinite) record retention
explanation: Rule 520-1-.08(6) requires a monthly written reconciliation of total trust liability against the bank balance, with reconciliation records kept for 3 years.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.08(4)(b), which of the following is a proper basis for a Georgia broker to disburse funds from the trust account?
choice_a: A verbal instruction from either party at any time
choice_b: The broker's own determination that the deal is unlikely to close, without any party's agreement
choice_c: Expiration of 90 days from deposit, regardless of the transaction's status
choice_d: Rejection of an offer, withdrawal of an unaccepted offer, closing, a signed written agreement of all interested parties, filing of an interpleader action, a court order, or a reasonable interpretation of the contract
explanation: Rule 520-1-.08(4)(b) enumerates the proper bases for disbursement: rejection of an offer, withdrawal of an unaccepted offer, closing, a signed written agreement of all interested parties, filing of an interpleader action, a court order, or reasonable contract interpretation.

question: A buyer submits an offer with earnest money held in the listing broker's trust account. The seller rejects the offer outright. Under Rule 520-1-.08(4)(b), has a proper basis for disbursement of the earnest money now arisen?
choice_a: Yes -- rejection of an offer is one of the enumerated proper bases for disbursement under Rule 520-1-.08(4)(b)
choice_b: No -- rejection of an offer never authorizes disbursement; only closing does
choice_c: No -- disbursement requires a court order regardless of the reason funds are held
choice_d: Yes, but only if 6 months have passed since the rejection
explanation: Rejection of an offer is explicitly listed among the proper disbursement triggers in Rule 520-1-.08(4)(b), so disbursement may proceed once the offer is rejected.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.08(4)(e), how must earnest money refunds be handled in Georgia?
choice_a: Only in cash, hand-delivered by the broker
choice_b: By check, or by credit to the party at closing
choice_c: Only by wire transfer directly from the buyer's lender
choice_d: Refunds are prohibited once funds are deposited into the trust account
explanation: Rule 520-1-.08(4)(e) requires earnest money refunds to be made by check or credited to the party at closing.

question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(4), how does Georgia law treat a broker's commingling of a principal's money or property with the broker's own funds?
choice_a: It is permitted as long as the broker discloses it verbally to the principal
choice_b: It is only a violation if the commingled amount exceeds $10,000
choice_c: It is an explicit, enumerated unfair trade practice subject to GREC discipline
choice_d: It is treated as a purely internal bookkeeping matter outside GREC's jurisdiction
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(4) explicitly enumerates commingling a principal's money or property with the licensee's own as an unfair trade practice ground for discipline.

question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(5), is a broker's failure to maintain a separate, federally-insured trust account (absent a written agreement otherwise) treated as a disciplinable offense?
choice_a: No -- it is only a civil matter between the broker and the affected party
choice_b: No -- Georgia law does not require a separate trust account in the first place
choice_c: Yes, but only if the broker also commingled funds at the same time
choice_d: Yes -- it is explicitly enumerated as an unfair trade practice ground for GREC discipline
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(5) explicitly lists failure to maintain a separate federally-insured trust account, absent written agreement otherwise, as an unfair trade practice ground for discipline -- independent of any commingling.
